subject: problem with VLC and save wav

messages.author: 02d83978ebd25181
messages.subject: problem with VLC and save wav
parts:
I am new to see wave (I am on Mac OS and R 3.1.2) and I have tried the following example:

# C major scale plot
     # C major scale sound
     # C major scale plot
     n <- 1:12
     freq <- notefreq(n)
     names <- c("C", "C#", "D", "D#", "E", "F", "F#", "G", "G#", "A", "A#", "B") 
     plot(n, freq, pch=19, cex=1.5,
          xlab = "Note name",
          ylab = "Frequency (Hz)",
          xaxt="n", las=1, main="Third octave")
     axis(side=1, at=n, labels=names)
     abline(h=freq, col="lightgrey")
     
     # C major scale sound
     f <- 2000 # sampling rate
     s <- NULL
     for (i in 1:length(freq))
       {
         tmp <- synth(d=0.5, f=f, cf=freq[i])
         s <- pastew(s, tmp, at="start", f)
       }
     spectro(s, f, ovlp=75)

I have then tried to listen to the sample and it works (mono):

listen(s,f=f)

I then saved the file using: 

savewav(s, f = f, filename = "test.wav")

I can play the file in iTunes but when I open it with VLC, it plays but there is no sound. I have then tried to play with writeWave  but I get the  following error:

'object' needs to be of class 'Wave' or 'WaveMC'

savewav(s, f = f, filename = "test.wav")

Any ideas? I am missing something? Would there be a possibility to save it in MP3 possibly in stereo?

Many thanks!

I have tried the following commands:

> new.S <- readWave("quick-learner.wav")

> new.S2 <- stereo(new.S,new.S)

Wave Object

Channels (Mono/Stereo): Stereo
PCM (integer format):   TRUE

> listen(new.S2)

It plays in iTunes but not in VLC (very strange as VLC can usually play anything that contains sound -- but I read that there may be a mono wav file problem).

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: problem with VLC and save wav
parts:
Dear Stephane,

Turning the frequency up to 44100 seems to work on my system (VLC, Ubuntu).

It seems that VLC may not be able to read any rate... To be confirmed.

The error you got with writeWave() was because synth() returns by
default a matrix, not a Wave or WaveMC object requested by write
Wave(). You can change this by using the argument out="Wave" in any
seewave function returning a sound or you can also use Wave() of tuneR
to coerce your final object into an appropriate Wave object.

HTH

Jerome
